messages:
alex: paging — infra alert fired: 5xx surge across ingress controller behind ALB in eastus-1. Notable: connection resets to upstreams, spike started ~ +80s ago. Pager went to oncall.

sre-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-0429
sre-bot: Severity: high
sre-bot: Affected service: api/redwood-ingress (eastus-1)

marta: I'm oncall and taking this. @lee @alex can you paste the quick topology? ALB -> k8s nodes (ingress-controller envoy) -> app pods?

lee: correct. ALB targets are node port targets (kube-proxy). Envoy sits as DaemonSet on each node. I'm seeing a bunch of Envoy logs:

```
[envoy] [warning] upstream reset while reading response: connection reset by peer (errno=104)
[envoy] cluster upstream timeout after 30s
```

lee: also seeing many 504s at ALB logs with target_response_count=0 for some requests.

alex: @marta second check: is this across all AZs or concentrated? Cloud metrics show elevated 5xx across eastus-1 but per-AZ delta — eastus-1b worse.

marta: running quick k8s checks — listing ingress pods and node distribution

```
kubectl get pods -n prod-ingress -o wide
NAME                         READY   STATUS    NODE
ingress-envoy-abc123         1/1     Running   node-a-eastus1a
ingress-envoy-def456         1/1     Running   node-b-eastus1b
ingress-envoy-ghi789         1/1     Running   node-c-eastus1b
```

marta: looks like more resets originating from nodes in eastus1b according to logs.

lee: checking node network errors:

```
ssh node-b-eastus1b
dmesg | tail
--> Rx buffer errors, link flaps reported around 12:40 UTC
```

marta: okay. Two parallel mitigation options:
- drain the affected nodes in eastus1b to shift traffic away from problematic hosts
- scale up ingress replicas in other AZs and let ALB re-balance

marta: going to cordon node-b-eastus1b and drain the envoy pod there. Will watch ALB targets.

alex: FYI we have customers reporting 5xx in dashboards. @chris please gather top impacted customers and their percent errors.

chris: on it. Quick query shows top 10 tenants saw 3–7% error rate increase, mostly API traffic behind /v1/generate. I'll open a customer-impact tracker doc.

marta: performed drain on node-b-eastus1b and restarted envoy on node-c as a precaution.

sre-bot: ACTION: node-b-eastus1b cordoned by marta at 1771009960

lee: ALB target health shows target group healthy counts dip by ~20% briefly then stabilize as ALB re-registers other nodes. Logs show connection resets drop after drain.

marta: scaled prod-ingress replicas from 3 -> 9 in AZs a and c to ensure capacity. Also temporarily reduced ALB connection idle timeout to 60s.

alex: any sign of DNS or cross-region routing change? Looks local to eastus region.

lee: no DNS changes. No changes in route53. Confirmed AWS console shows increased network errors on hosts in eastus-1b; opening AWS support case.

aws-support-bot: Support case 12345 opened with AWS — customer-reported networking flaps in eastus-1b. Engineer assigned.

marta: mitigation summary so far: node drain + restart + scale out. Observed 5xx rate drop from peak ~ 9% to ~1.2% baseline over 12 minutes. Rolling restarts in eastus1b still running.

chris: sent an interim status to the top impacted customers: short note, we are mitigating, will follow up with postmortem.

tara: I'm due for on-call handoff in ~20m. marta — want me to take over monitoring and postmortem once you finish triage?

marta: yes please @tara. I'll handoff the thread when I run the final checks. Leaving a checklist: verify ALB healthy hosts >= 95%, error rate back to baseline, no node network rx errors.

lee: also turned on more verbose envoy upstream logging for 10m window to capture any further resets.

sre-bot: NOTE: canary fallback to westus cluster is possible but heavy-handed; not recommended unless eastus region degrades for >2 hours.

marta: AWS engineer responded: 'we observed host-level NIC packet drops in eastus-1b starting 12:36 UTC and mitigations are rolling — ETA 45m for full hardware stabilization'. Link: https://aws.amazon.com/support/case/12345

marta: error rate stabilized to 0.9% now. ALB 5xx count trending down. Moving to monitoring-only state.

sre-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated (monitoring)

marta: handing off to @tara for observation and postmortem follow-up. Key notes for postmortem:
- Root cause: AWS host NIC packet drops in eastus-1b (AWS ticket)
- Impact: partial request failures (5xx) for ~18 minutes peak window
- Mitigations applied: cordon+drain affected nodes, scale up ingress in other AZs, restart envoy, adjusted ALB timeout temporarily
- Customer comms: interim notice sent; postmortem planned

tara: taking it. I'll keep monitoring for 60m and kick off postmortem doc with timeline + RCA. Assigning to marta for remediation notes and to lee for telemetry snippets.

chris: logging customer impact details into internal tracker and contacting account leads for most affected tenants.

marta: final check: no more connection resets in logs for last 8m, ALB target health back to normal. I'm marking this as resolved from my side.

sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED by marta at 1771011960 — will remain open for postmortem artifacts.

alex: thanks everyone for quick triage. We'll include a note about node-level network flaps and our mitigations in the postmortem. :thumbsup:

marta: adding AWS case number and supporting logs to the incident doc before handoff. Closing active paging."
